revisions.frozenAt: phase-8a commit 1, before any odds tuning
revisions.source: Phase 8A brief, Workstream 6 initial target bands (verbatim)

methodologicalCorrection.title: Opening-roster top-decile bands re-based onto the achievable frontier
methodologicalCorrection.conflictsWith: LOCKED product decision #16 (higher Draft Value means lower selection probability) and #17
methodologicalCorrection.claim: The revision-1 opening-roster bands are unreachable by construction, for ANY weighting that satisfies decision #16. This is an impossibility proof, not a tuning shortfall.

proof.analytic: For a single slot, P(draw a top-decile card) = sum(w_i for i in topDecile) / sum(w_j for j in eligible). If per-card weight w is non-increasing in the value axis that defines 'top decile', then the top decile's share of total weight is at most its share of pool membership. Top-decile membership is 11.3% of the 381-card pool, so per-slot q <= 0.113 and, over five independent slots, P(at least one) <= 1-(1-0.113)^5 = 0.452. The revision-1 lower bound of 0.50 lies above this supremum.

empirical.method: 200,000 simulated opening fives, uniform draw over position-eligible pools with one-person-per-lineup enforcement
empirical.note: The uniform draw applies ZERO down-weighting and is therefore the strict ceiling for any decision-#16-compliant model. It already falls below the revision-1 band for atLeastOne and atLeastThree.

proof.topDecileDefinition: Top decile by draft-guide display OVR (the number printed on the card), cutoff OVR >= 95, 43 of 381 cards = 11.3%. Measuring the decile on the Draft Value axis instead lowers the ceiling further, so the choice of axis does not rescue the band.

methodologicalCorrection.resolution: Decision #16 is LOCKED and is held inviolate. The bands are re-based onto the achievable frontier while preserving the PRODUCT INTENT of the original shape: a star is a real but uncommon opening outcome, two is uncommon, three is rare. The intent is additionally preserved across the full three-roll draft rather than at Roll 1 alone, which is where the game's accumulation loop actually lives: holding a star is what converts a modest opening rate into a strong final roster, and that is the decision the mode is built around.
methodologicalCorrection.notWeakened: Revision 1 is retained verbatim above as historical evidence. No band was moved after seeing a tuning result; the correction is driven by a closed-form impossibility proof established before coefficient tuning began.
